terms.gloss: play, dally, have one’s amorous fun
evidence: Plaut. Most. 5.2.36: scīs solēre illam aetātem tālī lūdō lūdere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives the sense “to sport, dally, wanton”. Traupman adds the partner with cum and the ablative; we have found no classical instance of cum with the verb in this sense, but the construction is the ordinary one for playing with someone.

phrases.latin: scīs solēre illam aetātem tālī lūdō lūdere
phrases.english: you know that at that age they like to play that kind of game

sources: Lewis & Short: ludo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 361.
